speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have symptoms of persistent vomiting and chest pain; to ensure your safety, could you please tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if you are currently experiencing any difficulty breathing or sweating?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture).

Based on the history of forceful vomiting, retching followed by choking, and subsequent chest pain in a 51-year-old male, this presentation is classic for an esophageal rupture. I am requesting a Chest X-Ray and a CT scan of the chest with oral contrast to confirm the diagnosis.
